vcu_0159_08001178.name: app_main_thunk
vcu_0159_08001178.summary: Tail-call thunk that jumps to the application main entry FUN_0800d858
vcu_0159_08001178.description: Two-instruction veneer that just calls FUN_0800d858 and returns. It is called from the C-runtime init routine (vcu_0159_080016ec, the scatter-load / __main equivalent) as the last step, so FUN_0800d858 is the application main(). Reset_Handler also calls FUN_0800d858 directly as a fallback after the runtime init returns. The one indirect call listed by the harness is the branch into main. Part of the startup group together with Reset_Handler and the runtime init.
vcu_0159_08001178.notes: That 0x0800d858 is main() is inferred from the call order in Reset_Handler and the runtime init, not from a string or symbol.

vcu_0159_08001188.name: Reset_Handler
vcu_0159_08001188.summary: Cortex-M reset vector: system init, C runtime init, then application main
vcu_0159_08001188.description: Reset entry (vector slot 1). Calls FUN_08008914 (clock / system initialisation, SystemInit-like), then FUN_080016ec (C-runtime init that copies/decompresses RAM sections and calls the main thunk), then FUN_0800d858 (application main) as a fallback if the runtime init ever returns. The initial stack pointer comes from vector slot 0 so the decompiler flags that SP may have been set. Startup group: Reset_Handler -> SystemInit-like -> scatter-load runtime -> app_main_thunk -> main.
vcu_0159_08001188.notes: The roles of FUN_08008914 as SystemInit and FUN_080016ec as scatterload/__main are inferred from order and callers.

vcu_0159_080011a2.name: Default_Handler
vcu_0159_080011a2.summary: Default trap for unused interrupt vectors: spins forever
vcu_0159_080011a2.description: Single instruction infinite loop (b .). The vector table points every unused exception and IRQ slot here; the harness labels it DMA2_Channel6_7_IRQHandler only because that is one of the slots referencing it. If an unexpected interrupt fires the MCU hangs until the watchdog (if enabled) resets it. Same role as the identical loop stubs in the older builds (the BusFault_Handler variants).

vcu_0159_0800120e.name: __aeabi_memcpy
vcu_0159_0800120e.summary: Forward memory copy: word-wise if both pointers 4-byte aligned, else bytewise
vcu_0159_0800120e.description: Compiler runtime memcpy (ARM EABI __aeabi_memcpy). If (dst|src)&3 is zero it copies 32-bit words while at least 4 bytes remain, then copies the remaining 0..3 bytes (or all bytes when either pointer is unaligned) one byte at a time. No overlap handling (forward copy only) and no return value. Used widely by the application (11 direct callers in this packet's callee view) for buffer and struct copies.

vcu_0159_08001232.name: __aeabi_memset
vcu_0159_08001232.summary: Fill a byte buffer with a constant value (dest, count, value argument order)
vcu_0159_08001232.description: Runtime memset helper in the ARM EABI argument order (dest, n, c), a plain byte loop that stores param_3 to param_2 consecutive bytes. The two short veneers right after it (vcu_0159_08001240 and vcu_0159_08001244) are its callers and are most likely __aeabi_memclr / __aeabi_memclr4 style wrappers that supply a zero value. No return value.

vcu_0159_08001256.name: __aeabi_fmul
vcu_0159_08001256.summary: Soft-float IEEE-754 single precision multiply (no FPU)
vcu_0159_08001256.description: Software float multiplication. Returns 0 if either operand has a zero magnitude. Otherwise adds the biased exponents (minus 0x7F), multiplies the 24-bit mantissas (implicit 1 | 23 bits) as a 64-bit product, normalises by one bit if needed, rounds to nearest-even and sets the sign to xor of the input signs. Underflow (negative exponent) flushes to +/-0 magnitude 0; overflow, infinities, NaN and denormals are not handled specially. The code is a Keil/ARM runtime routine used because the Cortex-M4 FPU is not enabled; called by the sensor/maths routines vcu_0159_08008cc0 and vcu_0159_08009240.
vcu_0159_08001256.notes: Sign of a zero result is dropped to +0 because the early-out returns 0.

vcu_14a_080012ba.name: __aeabi_i2f
vcu_14a_080012ba.summary: Soft-float convert signed 32-bit integer to single-precision float (VCU_14a build)
vcu_14a_080012ba.description: Takes the absolute value of the input (branch-free abs using the sign mask), normalises it with a count-leading-zeros shift, builds the exponent as 0x9D - clz (the mantissa top bit adds the final +1), packs sign, exponent and 23-bit mantissa, and rounds to nearest-even using the discarded low bits (round bit 0x80 with sticky 0x7F). Returns 0 for input 0. Exists only in the VCU_14a build; later builds use vcu_0159_080012e4 (unsigned) with a separate signed front end. Part of the soft-float runtime group.

vcu_0159_080012ba.name: __ARM_scalbnf
vcu_0159_080012ba.summary: Soft-float scale: add an integer to the exponent of a float (ldexpf style)
vcu_0159_080012ba.description: If the magnitude of param_1 is non-zero, checks that the biased exponent plus param_2 stays positive (-exp < n) and returns param_1 + (param_2 << 23), i.e. multiplies by 2^param_2 by adjusting the exponent field directly. Otherwise (result would underflow) returns 0; zero input is returned unchanged. No overflow or NaN/Inf checking. Called from vcu_0159_08009240 together with the other soft-float helpers. Different function from the VCU_14a function at the same address (which is int-to-float).
vcu_0159_080012ba.notes: Name is a best guess among ARM library helpers (scalbnf/ldexpf); behaviour is certain.

vcu_0159_080012e4.name: __aeabi_ui2f
vcu_0159_080012e4.summary: Soft-float convert unsigned 32-bit integer to single-precision float
vcu_0159_080012e4.description: Normalises the input with a count-leading-zeros shift, exponent = 0x9D - clz (+1 from the mantissa implicit bit), mantissa = top 24 bits, rounds to nearest-even from the low bits (round bit 0x80, sticky 0x7F). Returns 0 for 0. The signed wrapper (vcu_0159_080012d2, __aeabi_i2f) falls into/calls this routine after taking abs and re-applying the sign. Called from the same maths routines as the other soft-float helpers (vcu_0159_08008cc0, vcu_0159_08009240).

vcu_0159_080012ee.name: __aeabi_f2iz
vcu_0159_080012ee.summary: Soft-float convert single-precision float to signed int, truncating toward zero
vcu_0159_080012ee.description: Extracts the biased exponent and builds the 24-bit mantissa with implicit leading one. Exponent below 0x7F (|x| < 1) gives 0. Exponent below 0x97 shifts the mantissa right by 0x96 - exp, otherwise shifts left by exp - 0x96 (no saturation on overflow). If the sign bit is set the result is negated. Present from build 152 onward; called by vcu_0159_08009240.

vcu_0159_08001320.name: __aeabi_f2uiz
vcu_0159_08001320.summary: Soft-float convert float magnitude to unsigned int, truncating
vcu_0159_08001320.description: Same mantissa extraction and shifting as __aeabi_f2iz (right shift by 0x96 - exp for exp < 0x97, left shift otherwise, 0 if exp < 0x7F) but the sign bit is ignored, so negative inputs convert as their absolute value rather than clamping to 0. Called by vcu_0159_08009240.
vcu_0159_08001320.notes: Standard __aeabi_f2uiz would return 0 for negatives; this variant ignores the sign (may be a build-specific implementation).

vcu_0159_08001386.name: __aeabi_f2d
vcu_0159_08001386.summary: Soft-float widen single-precision float to double-precision (r0:r1 pair)
vcu_0159_08001386.description: Zero magnitude returns 0:0. Otherwise builds the double: sign bit kept, exponent = float exponent + 0x380 (1023-127) placed in bits 30..20 of the high word, mantissa top 20 bits (mantissa >> 3) in the high word and the low 3 mantissa bits shifted to the top of the low word (value << 29). Denormals, Inf and NaN are not special-cased. Called by vcu_0159_08008cc0.

returns.description: double bits, low word in r0, high word in r1

vcu_0159_080013ac.name: __aeabi_llsl
vcu_0159_080013ac.description: Compiler runtime helper for 64-bit shifts left. If the shift count is >= 32 the result high word is lo << (n-32) and low word 0, otherwise high = (hi << n) | (lo >> (32-n)) and low = lo << n. Used by the 64-bit/double arithmetic helpers vcu_0159_080011ac, vcu_0159_08001450 and vcu_0159_0800164e. Group: __aeabi_llsl / __aeabi_llsr / __aeabi_lasr.

vcu_0159_080013ca.name: __aeabi_llsr
vcu_0159_080013ca.description: Compiler runtime helper. Shift >= 32: low = hi >> (n-32), high = 0. Otherwise low = (lo >> n) | (hi << (32-n)), high = hi >> n. Called by the 64-bit/double helpers vcu_0159_080011ac, vcu_0159_08001348 and vcu_0159_0800164e. Group with __aeabi_llsl and __aeabi_lasr.

vcu_0159_080013ec.name: app_get_u16_2000329e
vcu_0159_080013ec.summary: Getter returning the 16-bit RAM variable at 0x2000329e
vcu_0159_080013ec.description: Returns DAT_2000329e unchanged. It sits in a block of five consecutive 16-bit getters (0x2000329c..0x200032a4: vcu_0159_080017c4, 080013ec, 08001410, 080017d0, 080017dc) that expose one 16-bit slot each, which looks like an array of sampled inputs (possibly ADC/DMA results or filtered sensor values) read by the main application loops vcu_0159_08003594, 08005938, 08007ecc and 080088f4, and one build-153 caller. What the value physically measures was not determinable from this function alone.
vcu_0159_080013ec.notes: Name is positional because the semantic of the variable is unknown; rename when the writer of 0x2000329e is annotated.

vcu_0159_080013fc.name: BusFault_Handler
vcu_0159_080013fc.summary: Bus fault exception handler: infinite loop
vcu_0159_080013fc.description: Single b . instruction. A bus fault (bad peripheral/memory access) halts the CPU here until the watchdog or a debugger intervenes. Present in builds 152, 153 and 159, where the fault handlers are separate stubs from the default handler.

vcu_0159_080013fe.name: DebugMon_Handler_v152_159
vcu_0159_080013fe.summary: Debug monitor exception handler: empty, returns immediately
vcu_0159_080013fe.description: Single bx lr. The debug monitor exception is not used by the application so the handler does nothing.

vcu_0159_08001410.name: app_get_u16_200032a0
vcu_0159_08001410.summary: Getter returning the 16-bit RAM variable at 0x200032a0
vcu_0159_08001410.description: Returns DAT_200032a0. Member of the five-entry 16-bit getter block starting at 0x2000329c (see app_get_u16_2000329e); called by vcu_0159_08003594, 08005938, 08007ecc and 080088f4, always alongside the 0x2000329e getter. Meaning of the value (probably a sampled/filtered analog input) is not established here.
vcu_0159_08001410.notes: Positional name; rename once the producer of 0x200032a0 is known.

vcu_0159_0800141c.name: EXINT0_IRQHandler_v152_159
vcu_0159_0800141c.summary: External interrupt line 0 handler: empty stub
vcu_0159_0800141c.description: Single bx lr. The interrupt is not serviced by the 152/153/159 builds, so the handler only returns. Pending flag in EXINT is not cleared, so if the line were enabled it would re-trigger; it is evidently left masked.

vcu_14a_0800141e.name: BusFault_Handler_v148_14a
vcu_14a_0800141e.summary: Bus fault handler in builds 148/14a: infinite loop
vcu_14a_0800141e.description: Single b . trap used as the BusFault vector in the VCU_148 and VCU_14a images. It is a different physical function (different family) from the BusFault_Handler of builds 152+, which moved because the code layout shifted; behaviour is identical. Halts the CPU on a bus fault.

vcu_0159_0800141e.name: EXINT9_5_IRQHandler_v152_159
vcu_0159_0800141e.summary: External interrupt lines 5..9 handler: empty stub
vcu_0159_0800141e.description: Single bx lr. The shared EXTI 9..5 vector is not used by this firmware (builds 152, 153, 159), so the handler returns without clearing any pending flag.

vcu_0159_08001436.name: app_level_complement_7
vcu_0159_08001436.summary: Return 7 minus the signed byte at offset 2 of a record
vcu_0159_08001436.description: Reads the signed char at param_1+2 and returns 7 - that value, i.e. mirrors a 0..7 level or index (for example converting an ascending step number into a descending one). Single caller vcu_0159_080047ac. The record layout and meaning of the field are not visible from this function.

params.name: param_1
params.description: pointer to a record whose byte +2 holds a small level value

vcu_0159_0800159e.name: __aeabi_lasr
vcu_0159_0800159e.description: Compiler runtime helper. Shift < 32: high = (s32)hi >> n, low = (lo >> n) | (hi << (32-n)). Shift >= 32: low = (s32)hi >> (n-32) and high is the sign fill (all ones or zeros). Called by vcu_0159_08001450 (double/64-bit arithmetic). Group with __aeabi_llsl and __aeabi_llsr.

returns.description: shifted value (low word r0, high r1)

vcu_0159_08001710.name: __scatterload_decompress
vcu_0159_08001710.summary: Decompress a packed section (literals, zero runs, back-references) into RAM
vcu_0159_08001710.description: Decompressor used by the Keil/ARM scatter-loader for compressed RW sections (no direct callers; it is invoked through a pointer from the load-region table, hence the indirect call). Each token starts with a header byte: low 3 bits give the literal count + 1 (if zero the next byte is the count), high nibble gives a run length (if zero the next byte supplies it). Literals are copied, then if header bit 3 is set it copies run+2 bytes from dest minus the following offset byte (LZ77 back-reference), otherwise it writes run zero bytes. Loops until dest reaches dst+size. Always returns 0.

params.name: param_3
params.description: number of output bytes to produce

vcu_0159_08001710.notes: Exact armlink compression scheme name (RLE vs LZ77 variant) not confirmed; token semantics derived directly from the code.

vcu_0159_080017c4.name: app_get_u16_2000329c
vcu_0159_080017c4.summary: Getter returning the 16-bit RAM variable at 0x2000329c
vcu_0159_080017c4.description: Returns DAT_2000329c. First element of the five consecutive 16-bit getters (0x2000329c..0x200032a4). Called by vcu_0159_08003594 and vcu_0159_08005938 only. Meaning not determinable from this function; likely a sampled analog input.

vcu_0159_080017d0.name: app_get_u16_200032a2
vcu_0159_080017d0.summary: Getter returning the 16-bit RAM variable at 0x200032a2
vcu_0159_080017d0.description: Returns DAT_200032a2. Part of the 0x2000329c.. array of 16-bit values. Sole caller is vcu_0159_080042f8, which also calls the next getter (0x200032a4) and the TMR2 output disable routine.

vcu_0159_080017dc.name: app_get_u16_200032a4
vcu_0159_080017dc.summary: Getter returning the 16-bit RAM variable at 0x200032a4
vcu_0159_080017dc.description: Returns DAT_200032a4. Last of the five 16-bit getter functions over 0x2000329c..0x200032a4. Sole caller is vcu_0159_080042f8.

vcu_0159_080017e8.name: app_apply_mode_limits
vcu_0159_080017e8.summary: Load 16-bit parameter pairs into the config block according to the mode in 0x20001fa7
vcu_0159_080017e8.description: Switch on the byte DAT_20001fa7 (modes 0..6, other values use the default). Every mode writes DAT_20001b38 = 3, DAT_20001b3a = DAT_20001b3c = 0x0505 (5,5), a pair 0x140F (20,15) or 0x190F (25,15) into DAT_20001b3e and DAT_20001b42, and a second pair into DAT_20001b40 and DAT_20001b44: 0x1919 (25,25) for modes 0 and 5/default, 0x1414 (20,20) for mode 2, 0x2828 (40,40) for mode 3, 0x2020 (32,32) for modes 4 and 6, and for mode 1 either 0x2020 or 0x1919 depending on bit 4 of DAT_20001b32. It also adjusts flag bits in DAT_20001aee: bit 3 (0x0008) is set only in mode 3 and cleared otherwise, and bit 12 (0x1000) is cleared in all modes except 0, 3, 4 and 6. Appears to select per-ride-mode limit/threshold pairs (byte pairs, units unknown); called from vcu_0159_08009da8 and vcu_0159_0800b294.
vcu_0159_080017e8.notes: Mapping of mode numbers to ride modes and the physical meaning of the byte pairs are unconfirmed.

vcu_0159_08001b14.name: util_hex_char_to_nibble
vcu_0159_08001b14.summary: Convert an ASCII hex digit to its value 0..15, 0 for invalid characters
vcu_0159_08001b14.description: Accepts '0'-'9', 'A'-'F' and 'a'-'f'. Digits subtract 0x30, upper-case letters subtract 0x37, lower-case letters subtract 0x57, result masked to 8 bits. Any other character returns 0 (no error indication). Called from vcu_0159_08006d6c, which presumably parses hex text (e.g. an ASCII command or ID string).

returns.description: nibble value 0..15, 0 if not a hex digit

vcu_0159_08001b46.name: util_interp_linear_clamp_hi
vcu_0159_08001b46.summary: Linear interpolation between (x0,yB) and (x1,yA), clamped to yA above x1
vcu_0159_08001b46.description: With x=param_1, x0=param_2, x1=param_3, yA=param_4, yB=param_5: if x > x1 returns yA; otherwise returns yB - (yB - yA)*(x - x0)/(x1 - x0) using signed integer arithmetic (division truncates toward zero). So the output goes from yB at x0 to yA at x1 along a straight line, with no clamp below x0 (extrapolates). No guard against x1 == x0, which would divide by zero when x == x1. Single caller vcu_0159_08009240, a numeric sensor/mapping routine that also uses the soft-float helpers.

params.name: param_4
params.description: yA output at and above x1

vcu_0159_08001b64.name: app_set_state
vcu_0159_08001b64.summary: Set the application state byte and reset its sub-step counter when it changes
vcu_0159_08001b64.description: If param_1 differs from the state byte DAT_2000101a, stores the new value (low 8 bits) and zeroes DAT_2000101c (the sub-state / step or timer counter belonging to that state). Setting the same state again is a no-op so the counter keeps running. Called from more than a dozen state handlers (vcu_0159_0800193c, 080029f4, 08002fc0, 08003254, 080032c4, 08003444, 080038a4, 08003c5c, 080046c0, 080047ac, 080051e8, 080054ec ...), so these form the main application state machine and this is its transition primitive.
vcu_0159_08001b64.notes: Whether DAT_2000101c is a step index or a tick counter is not established (written as 0 only).

vcu_0159_08001b78.name: tmr2_pwm_set_frequency
vcu_0159_08001b78.summary: Start TMR2 channel 1 PWM at a given frequency (Hz) with 3/4 compare value
vcu_0159_08001b78.description: Clears TMR2.CTRL1.TMREN (bit 0) to stop the counter, writes period PR (0x4000002C) = 1000000 / param_1 and channel-1 compare C1DT (0x40000034) = PR - PR/4 (75% of the period), resets the counter CVAL (0x40000024) to 0 and re-enables the timer. The period arithmetic assumes the timer counts at 1 MHz (prescaler set elsewhere), so param_1 is a frequency in Hz; param_1 = 0 would divide by zero. Looks like a buzzer / tone generator; sole caller is vcu_0159_08001ba8, and vcu_0159_08001bbc switches the output off. Output enable is separate (TMR2.CCTRL).

params.name: param_1
params.description: output frequency in Hz (timer assumed 1 MHz)

vcu_0159_08001b78.notes: Buzzer use and the 1 MHz timer clock are inferred; duty polarity depends on the TMR2 channel mode set at init.

vcu_0159_08001bbc.name: tmr2_pwm_output_disable
vcu_0159_08001bbc.summary: Clear TMR2 capture/compare enable bit 0 to turn the channel-1 output off
vcu_0159_08001bbc.description: Read-modify-write of the register at 0x40000020 (TMR2.CCTRL): clears bit 0 (C1EN), disabling the channel 1 compare output while leaving the counter running. Counterpart of tmr2_pwm_set_frequency (the enable bit is set elsewhere, presumably in the caller of that routine). Called from vcu_0159_08002d64, 080042f8, 08006b24 and 0800a39c.
vcu_0159_08001bbc.notes: Harness decoded the register as TMR2.CCTRL; buzzer/tone output is a guess from the paired frequency routine.

vcu_148_0800252e.name: BusFault_Handler_v148
vcu_148_0800252e.summary: Bus fault handler in VCU_148: infinite loop
vcu_148_0800252e.description: Single b . trap at 0x0800252e of the VCU_148 image, referenced by the vector table as BusFault_Handler (in this build it is a separate loop stub from the one at 0x0800141e). Hangs the CPU on any bus fault. Behaviourally identical to the BusFault handlers of other builds.

vcu_14f_080028be.name: BusFault_Handler_v14b_14f
vcu_14f_080028be.summary: Bus fault handler in builds 14b/14e/14f: infinite loop
vcu_14f_080028be.description: Single b . trap at 0x080028be used as BusFault vector in VCU_14b, VCU_14e and VCU_14f. Hangs the CPU on a bus fault; identical in behaviour to the other BusFault_Handler variants, only its address and therefore family differ.

vcu_0159_08002998.name: app_verify_uid_checksum
vcu_0159_08002998.summary: Check that a two-word record equals the complement of sum and product of three RAM words
vcu_0159_08002998.description: Computes s = DAT_20001c68 + DAT_20001c6c + DAT_20001c70 and p = DAT_20001c68 * DAT_20001c6c * DAT_20001c70 (32-bit wrap) and returns 1 only if param_1[0] == ~s and param_1[1] == ~p, else 0. The three RAM words are most likely the 96-bit device-ID copied from 0x1FFFF7E8 at startup, and the 8-byte record a stored licence/pairing value, so this is an anti-copy / per-device binding check. Single caller vcu_0159_080054ec (also a state-machine step calling app_set_state).

params.name: param_1
params.description: pointer to two u32 words: ~sum and ~product

vcu_0159_08002998.notes: That 0x20001c68..70 hold the chip UID is inferred from the brief; not verified in this packet.
